items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: Charlie Reynolds is taking over old man Baron's, Ben Allen's, rather, old man Ben Allen's place... he said, 'Sam, you can bring a band in here.'

ctx.x: Now, when I come back from Detroit, a man, a fellow come to me and he said, "Sam, what are you doing?" And I said, "We just got back into town. We're not doing anything." Well, he said, "Charlie Reynolds is taking over old man Baron's, Ben Allen's, rather, old man Ben Allen's place." Now let me tell you about Ben Allen. Ben Allen was a -- there was two negroes in Atlantic City at that time that controlled the whole negro section. One was Ben Allen, and then, up North, up in the other part of the town, there was…

Now, these two fellows could HANDLE on any part of the sporting world and they could control anything that went on down there. But Ben Allen was getting old now, and he was tired of this business, so he turned the place over to Charley Reynolds. But Charley Reynolds was a younger fellow and he had his gambling going there and everything, so he wanted a good show. He figured that being at Kentucky and Arctic Avenue, that was the hub of the black belt. Where everybody, both the people who were good and the people…

See, so, he said, 'Sam, you can bring a band in here.' I had about, let's see, I had five, six musicians at that time. He said, 'Come on in here and find me some girls that are good entertainers. And a man to go along with them.' So, that's when I picked up the two Ethels and another girl named Izzy Ringgold, which was a very good dancer and singer. In fact, she outsung most of the girls at that time. She was very good. And then I had a fellow called Snow Fisher.
